text:
carla: raising from a customer ticket — Acme reports SSO logins failing for their users after a scheduled IdP cert rotation. Their engineers say it started right after the rotation window. Error from their side: "SAML Response: Assertion signature invalid / Audience restriction mismatch". they shared the IdP metadata XML. attaching what they pasted below.

nikhil: can you paste the IdP metadata URL and the ACS entity we're currently serving for them? also any recent deploys to the saml/handler? :eyes:

carla: pasted the IdP metadata (truncated):
```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme.example/">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo>...CERT (PEM encoded) ...</KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <SingleSignOnService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Redirect" Location="https://idp.acme.example/sso/saml"/>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
Their ACS in their IdP shows `https://console.redwood.ai/saml/acs?tenant=acme`. but our metadata currently published says `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/redirect` for that tenant — possible mismatch. They also included our earlier fingerprint which doesn't match the new cert in their metadata.

jonah: hmm we had a config change in last deploy that normalized ACS paths to `/saml/acs/redirect` (to support new routing). That should have been backwards-compatible but looks like some IdPs are sensitive to exact ACS URL/audience. i see a deploy-bot entry: `deploy-bot: saml-handler v2.14 -> canary -> prod at 1745121200`

marta: @carla thanks for the heads-up. if it's an audience mismatch that's on us to either publish old SP metadata or add the alternate ACS as a valid audience. can we repro locally against their IdP metadata?

carla: reproduced with their metadata using our SAML test harness (attached logs):
```
SAML AuthnRequest -> sent to IdP
SAML Response <- 302 with SAMLResponse (base64)
Validate signature -> FAIL: unverified signature (certificate fingerprint mismatch)
Validate audience -> FAIL: expected https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/redirect, got https://console.redwood.ai/saml/acs?tenant=acme
```
They also tried refreshing the IdP metadata after rotation; no change.

nikhil: two likely causes: 1) our SP metadata served to them is stale (old entityID/Audience) or 2) they are still sending assertions to the old ACS (console.redwood.ai) while we expect app.redwood.ai. we need to check the `saml-handler` config for tenant-level overrides stored in the tenant config store (S3/DB). i'll check ACLs on the config bucket — there was a worker that tried to rotate certs last night.

idp-monitor-bot: automated alert — certificate rotation job failed for tenant `acme` at 1745122005: S3 PutObjectAccessDenied (403).

nikhil: that bot entry explains a lot. the cert rotation job ran but couldn't upload updated SP metadata into the tenant bucket due to a perms regression in a recent infra change. so the IdP got the new IdP cert but our published SP metadata remained the old one — mismatch. i can confirm `s3://redwood-tenant-config/acme/saml/metadata.xml` has last-modified 1745119000 (pre-rotation).

carla: the customer said they rotated the IdP cert and then logs started showing `Assertion signature invalid`. makes sense if IdP started using new signing cert but we still had old SP metadata referencing the old cert. but why is the ACS URL different?

jonah: separate issue — our canary changed the canonical SP entityID/ACS to `https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs/redirect` and upstream console uses `console.redwood.ai` hostname in the redirect flow. Some IdPs validate the Audience exactly and won't accept alternate hostnames, even if we accept both on our end. we should add both inbound audiences for the tenant as a quick fix, and re-run the metadata upload.

marta: agreed. quick remediation plan: 1) re-upload correct tenant SP metadata to S3 (with both ACS URLs in AssertionConsumerService entries and updated cert fingerprints), 2) if S3 permissions still block, provision a manual override in the admin console to update tenant metadata, 3) roll back the canary change if necessary for the tenant group. can we get a repro-after-fix check from the customer?

nikhil: i'm patching the S3 ACLs now. also adding a defensive check to the rotation worker to stop on 403 and page. will push a one-line fix and then attempt metadata upload. command i'll run: 
```bash
aws s3 cp acme-sp-metadata.xml s3://redwood-tenant-config/acme/saml/metadata.xml --acl bucket-owner-full-control
```

carla: note — customer attempted to upload new IdP cert into our console and got a 400 with `Invalid PEM format`. their dev pasted the PEM and i noticed there are stray spaces and a wrapped header line. they were able to work around by running `sed -n '1,200p' idp.pem > cleaned.pem` and reuploading. if we want to improve UX we should do a server-side PEM normalization step.

nikhil: upload succeeded after ACL fix. metadata now updated at 1745123800. i also added alternate ACS `https://console.redwood.ai/saml/acs?tenant=acme` as an allowed Audience for the tenant and included both ACS endpoints in the SP metadata.

support-bot: note saved to ticket #238612: tenant `acme` metadata updated and cert rotation retried.

carla: i asked customer to retry login. they ran an IdP-initiated test and reported back: `Login succeeded!` they provided logger output showing signature verification ok and audience matching the console ACS.

marta: follow-ups: 
- We should add a pre-rotation checklist for tenants that do strict audience checks (notify to add alternate ACS urls) and warn them of exact-Audience enforcement.
- Add PEM normalization on upload and a clearer error message that suggests `sed` cleanup.
- Add a canary gating rule so that SP entityID/ACS changes don't roll out until tenant metadata confirmed.

jonah: created a small PR to include both ACS variants in the tenant metadata generator and a check that prevents automatic SP entityID mutation unless a tenant-level opt-in flag is set. PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/saml-handler/pull/812

nikhil: i'll follow up later with the ACL audit and the fix to the rotation worker to page on 403 rather than silently failing. logged infra task INFRA-842.

carla: closing the slack thread once ticket is marked resolved. thanks everyone — good cross-team response. :party_parrot:
